cohort: 38 women who underwent sacrococcygeal teratoma resection after 1970 in one of six pediatric surgical centers in the Netherlands
finding: Resection of a sacrococcygeal teratoma in female patients does not appear to negatively impact fertility, and vaginal delivery is achievable and safe for both mother and child.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery was successful in the majority of cases (17 out of 20), indicating that caesarean section is not necessarily the default mode of delivery for women with a history of sacrococcygeal teratoma resection.
